question: Why can tiny on-surface changes to sparse point-cloud conditions make leading 3D diffusion Transformers switch from a connected reconstruction to hundreds of fragments, where in the encoder/denoiser is that failure committed, and can a localized test-time spectral intervention prevent it without retraining?

key_findings.claim: Adaptive on-surface search finds the Meltdown transition for most WaLa shapes and every tested Make-A-Shape subset shape, but these rates measure adversarially discoverable susceptibility rather than natural failure incidence.
key_findings.evidence: On full WaLa evaluation sets, 926/1,030 GSO shapes (89.9%) and 352/381 SimJEB shapes (92.4%) admit a perturbation changing a connected output into fragments. Make-A-Shape search succeeds on 130/130 stratified GSO subset shapes and 30/30 SimJEB subset shapes. Each trial starts from the smallest sparse Poisson sample producing a healthy output, constructs a jittered/reprojected cloud, and brackets then bisects the interpolation to the first C>1 outcome.

key_findings.claim: On a controlled sphere, classical point-uniformity energy is a strong input-side predictor of Meltdown and the point encoder preserves the relevant distinction rather than creating it.
key_findings.evidence: Across 1,437 unique Riesz-tested clouds and five diffusion seeds (7,185 passes), none of 675 runs below normalized energy difference 0.01 melt, 762/765 runs above 0.20 melt, and the 50% crossing is near 0.07. Across 1,434 encoder pairs, energy yields AUC 0.981-0.995 and encoder-output drift 0.974-0.982, while intermediate encoder representations remain within 0.01 AUC; per-point stages amplify melt/healthy drift 5.6-6.8x and the multi-head-attention bottleneck compresses this to 2.1-2.4x without eliminating it.

anchors.section: Appendix F / Layerwise and residualized probes

key_findings.claim: The melt-relevant encoder signal is structurally encoded and not reducible to a linearly readable scalar uniformity score.
key_findings.evidence: A linear PCA-based regression from encoder output to the Riesz statistic has cross-validated R2 from -0.18 to 0.09, whereas logistic probes classify melt with AUC 0.974-0.981. After linearly residualizing representations against Riesz energy, classification remains high at AUC 0.864-0.937, so the representation carries information beyond that one scalar.

key_findings.claim: Healthy-to-unhealthy activation patching localizes a unique full-quality rescue handle to the cross-attention output write at WaLa block 4 on the first denoising step.
key_findings.evidence: The initial 32 blocks x 8 steps x 2 conditioning-site scan isolates Y_4,7. The appendix extends this to all 19 within-block activations—4,864 patches per seed over three seeds—and finds that only the cross-attention output write gives canonical full-quality rescue; self-attention, AdaLN, and cross-attention pre-write sites give none, while downstream residual/block-output sites carry the already written signal. Canonical patch Chamfer is 0.0886 +/- 0.0001 versus 0.0916 for the clean reference, and downstream propagation patches give 0.0896 +/- 0.0014.

key_findings.claim: The localized cross-attention output is sufficient as a rescue lever but is not, in isolation, sufficient to cause the failure in the reverse direction.
key_findings.evidence: Transplanting healthy Y_4,7 into an unhealthy run rescues, but transplanting the corresponding unhealthy write into a healthy run produces 0/256 Meltdowns over Y cells and 0/768 over cross-attention write sites. Bidirectional effects first appear at block outputs and cumulative residual state. The paper's stronger language that the single write 'commits' the trajectory therefore describes a context-dependent causal handle, not a self-contained necessary-and-sufficient circuit.

key_findings.claim: Matched controls support a directional, low-rank drift account of the WaLa write, while scalar spectral entropy is only a correlated diagnostic.
key_findings.evidence: Subtracting the write's projection onto the top 20 singular directions of healthy-to-unhealthy drift rescues 100/100 seeds with one component and Chamfer 0.0887. Four matched controls—drift-orthogonal random directions, scalar attenuation, Gaussian perturbation, and removal of the activation's own leading singular components—produce 0/3,200 rescues. Directional rescue has spectral entropy 1.613, while scalar attenuation, random, Gaussian, and keep-top controls span 1.582-1.884 yet all fail, falsifying entropy magnitude as the causal variable.

key_findings.claim: Make-A-Shape exposes an analogous but architecture-specific spectral signature: the tail carries the melt component and the leading singular signal remains necessary for reconstruction.
key_findings.evidence: At the transition midpoint across 100 seeds, baseline rescue is 25/100 with mean component count 124.9. Keeping only the top 5 or 10 singular components rescues 99/100 with mean C 2.75/2.67, whereas removing leading components rescues only 4-8/100 and worsens mean C to 156.8-165.5. Thus a simple universal rule such as 'remove top rank' is contradicted; the effective intervention depends on which architecture's spectrum contains failure signal.

key_findings.claim: PowerRemap converts the mechanistic observation into a high-rate test-time rescue for WaLa and a lower, per-shape-selected rescue rate for Make-A-Shape.
key_findings.evidence: PowerRemap leaves singular vectors fixed and maps each singular value to sigma_i^gamma / sigma_1^(gamma-1). With gamma=100 at the localized WaLa site, it rescues 910/926 GSO failures (98.3%) and 344/352 SimJEB failures (97.7%). Searching gamma per shape for Make-A-Shape rescues 110/130 GSO failures (84.6%) and 25/30 SimJEB failures (83.3%); median effective gamma is 1.10 (SD 0.13) and 1.05 (SD 0.063), respectively.

key_findings.claim: The rescue is highly site-specific, but the evidence that it is harmless on already healthy inputs is extremely narrow.
key_findings.evidence: A 512-site cross-attention/MLP sweep (768 sites including the prior self-attention scan) finds only four rescue sites, three high quality at t=7 and one degraded site at t=0, a reported specificity near 0.5%. Conversely, the no-harm check covers only one SimJEB shape, ten seeds, and gamma in {2,5,10,100}; topology remains connected in all 40 runs, which cannot estimate population-level false interventions or geometry degradation.

key_findings.claim: Diffusion ensembles show delayed symmetry breaking after the early write, consistent with a bifurcation account but not a quantitative proof of one.
key_findings.evidence: Across 100 noise seeds over the interpolation path, intermediate conditions produce both healthy and fragmented endpoints and expected C changes smoothly. At rho=0.4, a fixed 2D projection of 1,000 trajectories is not detectably non-unimodal at the initial step (adjusted dip-test p=1), rejects unimodality from the fifth plotted step (p=4.5e-3), and then yields p<1e-4. Because Y is written at the first denoising step and the population separates later, the timing is compatible with an upstream perturbation crossing a basin boundary, but no Hessian, Lyapunov exponent, or projection-invariant bifurcation statistic is measured.

key_findings.claim: Deployment-fair preprocessing, noise injection, and small best-of-K sampling baselines do not rescue the canonical sphere failure, although some reduce fragmentation severity.
key_findings.evidence: WLOP yields 0/48 rescues across 1, 2, 5, and 15 iterations; two iterations improve Voronoi coefficient of variation from 0.517 to 0.422 but remain fragmented, while 15 iterations nearly collapse pairwise arcs and explode Riesz energy. Variance-preserving conditioning noise gives 0/96 rescues and best-of-K up to four samples gives 0/24, for 0/168 deployment-fair rescues total. PowerRemap rescues all six matched canonical seeds with C=1, Chamfer 0.0887, and sphericity 1.0001. These baselines are narrow six-seed stress tests, not dataset-scale competitors.

anchors.section: Appendix H.1 / Uniformity and collapse diagnostics

method.core_idea: Construct controlled healthy-to-fragmented point-cloud paths, follow the perturbation from input statistics through the encoder and diffusion backbone, use exhaustive causal activation swaps and matched directional controls to localize the context-dependent commit handle, then reshape that activation's singular spectrum at test time.
method.mechanism: For a sphere, clean Fibonacci point sets and Gaussian-jittered points reprojected to the surface are connected by spherical interpolation; WaLa uses N=400 and Make-A-Shape N=1,200 with a shared terminal-noise seed across the path. For real meshes, Poisson-sampled healthy clouds are perturbed and projected back to the oracle surface, then geometric bracketing and bisection find the first interpolation value with more than one output component. Riesz s=2 energy and encoder probes trace input nonuniformity. Healthy activations are patched into unhealthy WaLa runs over a block-by-denoising-time grid and, in the appendix, all 19 submodule activations. SVD-based drift surgery and magnitude-matched controls identify a low-rank directional signal. PowerRemap performs a local SVD of the early cross-attention output, keeps singular vectors, and exponentiates normalized singular values with gamma >= 1. Diffusion trajectories across random noise are projected and tested for delayed multimodality.
assumptions: Connected-component count on a fixed extraction grid is an adequate primary indicator of healthy versus Meltdown output.
On-surface jitter and mesh reprojection approximate plausible sparse-point variation despite requiring oracle knowledge of the underlying surface.
The first adversarially found connected-to-fragmented transition on an interpolation path is representative enough for mechanistic localization.
Activation patching between matched healthy and unhealthy runs isolates behavior-relevant causal carriers despite off-manifold hybrid internal states.
The top singular directions of healthy-to-unhealthy activation drift are stable causal coordinates rather than artifacts of one shape, seed, or normalization.
A local SVD remapping at one identified site preserves intended geometry while suppressing the failure component.
The 2D projection used for trajectory ensembles retains the separation relevant to the proposed bifurcation.
Mechanisms found mainly on WaLa sphere paths meaningfully transfer to real shapes and to the shallower Make-A-Shape cross-attention architecture.
Per-shape gamma search is an acceptable evaluation of rescue potential even though it is not a pre-calibrated deployment rule.

techniques.role: Defines healthy output as C=1 and failure as C>1 after extracting the generated surface on a 0.05 grid.
Interpolates between clean and jittered/reprojected clouds while keeping every point on the sphere or mesh, isolating distributional layout from gross off-surface corruption.
Finds a healthy sparse cloud, constructs a perturbed endpoint, geometrically brackets the topology change, and bisects to the smallest failure-inducing interpolation.
Quantifies point-cloud nonuniformity and supplies a high-AUC input-side diagnostic on controlled spheres.
Measures drift amplification/compression and uses scalar regression, melt classification, and residualization to distinguish a structural representation from a one-number encoding.
Swaps matched healthy activations into unhealthy runs across 32 WaLa blocks, eight denoising steps, and ultimately 19 within-block sites to localize rescue.
Transplants unhealthy activations into healthy runs to test whether the localized rescue handle is also sufficient to induce failure.
Subtracts projections onto leading singular directions of the healthy-to-unhealthy write drift and contrasts them with drift-orthogonal, attenuation, Gaussian, and own-basis controls.
Tracks spectrum flattening across the transition while matched controls demonstrate that the scalar entropy itself is not the intervention target.
Applies sigma_i' = sigma_i^gamma / sigma_1^(gamma-1) at the localized write, preserving the leading singular value and vectors while suppressing the relative tail without retraining.
Runs 100- and 1,000-seed ensembles, projects trajectories, and applies Hartigan's dip test to locate delayed population splitting after the early conditioning write.
Tests WLOP resampling, variance-preserving conditioning noise, and best-of-K sampling under no-retraining/no-oracle-at-deployment constraints.

evaluations.setting: Pages 7-8, Table 1 — WaLa with adaptive on-surface search over complete GSO (1,030 shapes) and SimJEB (381 shapes) sets
evaluations.metric: Shapes with an adversarially discoverable Meltdown; PowerRemap rescue among failures
evaluations.result: GSO: 926/1,030 failures (89.9%) and 910/926 rescued at gamma=100 (98.3%). SimJEB: 352/381 failures (92.4%) and 344/352 rescued (97.7%).
evaluations.baseline: Original WaLa DDIM/DDPM reconstruction without an internal activation intervention.

evaluations.setting: Pages 7-8, Table 1 — Make-A-Shape on stratified GSO (130 shapes) and SimJEB (30 shapes) subsets with 100 denoising steps
evaluations.metric: Shapes with an adversarially discoverable Meltdown; rescue after per-shape gamma search
evaluations.result: GSO: 130/130 failures and 110/130 rescued (84.6%). SimJEB: 30/30 failures and 25/30 rescued (83.3%). Median effective gamma is 1.10 +/- 0.13 SD on GSO and 1.05 +/- 0.063 on SimJEB.
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified Make-A-Shape; full-corpus evaluation is not run because of the longer sampler.

evaluations.setting: Pages 49-50, Appendix E — controlled sphere, 1,437 unique clouds at N=400/500/600 and five seeds (7,185 forward passes)
evaluations.metric: Meltdown frequency versus normalized Riesz s=2 energy difference
evaluations.result: 0/675 runs melt below DeltaE=0.01; 762/765 (99.6%) melt above 0.20; the empirical 50% crossing is near 0.07. A path point at rho=0.05 has DeltaE about 0.18 and roughly 73 components.
evaluations.baseline: Lower-energy, more uniformly distributed on-sphere clouds.

evaluations.setting: Pages 50-51, Appendix F — 1,434 sphere clouds, 484 melting and 950 healthy
evaluations.metric: ROC AUC and cross-validated R2 for input and encoder probes
evaluations.result: Riesz energy AUC 0.981-0.995; encoder-output drift AUC 0.974-0.982; logistic melt probe AUC 0.974-0.981 and 0.864-0.937 after linear Riesz residualization; scalar DeltaE regression R2 -0.18 to 0.09.
evaluations.baseline: Input energy alone, intermediate encoder layers, and linear scalar readout from PCA features.

evaluations.setting: Pages 44-49, Appendix D — WaLa 32 blocks x 8 denoising steps x 19 activation sites, three seeds
evaluations.metric: Connected rescue and reconstruction Chamfer after activation replacement
evaluations.result: The cross-attention output Y_4,7 is the unique canonical full-quality within-block rescue; canonical patch Chamfer 0.0886 +/- 0.0001, clean reference 0.0916, downstream propagation 0.0896 +/- 0.0014, and off-canonical MLP pockets 0.0967-0.0981.
evaluations.baseline: Self-attention, AdaLN, cross-attention pre-write, MLP, and residual/block-output patches over the same depth-time grid.

evaluations.setting: Pages 48-49, Appendix D.4 — reverse transplant from unhealthy to healthy WaLa runs
evaluations.result: 0/256 Y-cell transplants and 0/768 cross-attention-write transplants induce Meltdown; block outputs and cumulative residual state, not the isolated Y write, first show bidirectional effects.
evaluations.baseline: The healthy-to-unhealthy rescue direction, in which patching Y_4,7 is sufficient to restore connectivity.

evaluations.setting: Pages 39-43, Appendix C — WaLa targeted drift surgery at the localized write over 100 seeds plus matched controls
evaluations.metric: Rescue rate, component count, Chamfer, and spectral entropy
evaluations.result: Removing the top 10 drift directions rescues 76/100 and top 20 or 50 rescues 100/100, reaching C=1 and Chamfer 0.0887. Four control families total 0/3,200 rescues despite matched magnitude and overlapping entropy values.
evaluations.baseline: Drift-orthogonal random subspaces (0/1,200), scalar attenuation (0/400), Gaussian perturbations (0/1,200), and removal of the write's own leading components (0/400).

evaluations.setting: Pages 39-40, Appendix C.1 — Make-A-Shape midpoint at rho=0.5 over 100 diffusion seeds
evaluations.metric: Connected rescue rate and mean component count under spectral truncation
evaluations.result: Baseline 25/100 and mean C=124.9; keep-top-5 99/100 and C=2.75; keep-top-10 99/100 and C=2.67; removing leading components rescues only 4-8/100 and raises C to 156.8-165.5.
evaluations.baseline: Unmodified write and symmetric top-removal versus tail-removal interventions.

evaluations.setting: Page 52, Appendix G — spectral remapping at 512 cross-attention/MLP depth-time sites (768 when the prior self-attention scan is included)
evaluations.metric: Sites that rescue connectivity and preserve shape quality
evaluations.result: Only four sites rescue; three high-quality sites occur at t=7 (cross-attention blocks 4 and 3, MLP block 0), and one low-quality MLP block-0 site occurs at t=0, for about 0.5% site-level specificity.
evaluations.baseline: The same remapping applied at every other scanned activation.

evaluations.setting: Pages 8-10, Section 5 — 100-seed interpolation ensembles and 1,000 trajectories at rho=0.4 under a fixed 2D projection
evaluations.metric: Expected component count and Hartigan dip-test adjusted p-value over denoising time
evaluations.result: Intermediate inputs yield both attractors; unimodality is not rejected initially (p=1), is rejected from the fifth plotted step (p=4.5e-3), and is strongly rejected thereafter (p<1e-4).
evaluations.baseline: A single deterministic-looking path or an always-bimodal trajectory population.

evaluations.setting: Pages 53-57, Appendix H — canonical WaLa sphere stress case with deployment-fair controls
evaluations.metric: Connected rescue count plus geometry/uniformity diagnostics
evaluations.result: WLOP 0/48, conditioning noise 0/96, and best-of-K <=4 0/24, totaling 0/168; PowerRemap rescues 6/6 matched seeds with C=1, Chamfer 0.0887, and sphericity 1.0001. WLOP can improve Voronoi COV 0.517 to 0.422 without rescue, and aggressive noise can reduce C without reaching one.
evaluations.baseline: Input resampling, stochastic conditioning perturbation, and sampling more unmodified trajectories.

evaluations.setting: Page 38, Appendix B.6 — no-harm check on one already healthy SimJEB shape (ID 492), ten seeds, gamma 2/5/10/100
evaluations.baseline: The same healthy shape without intervention; no multi-shape false-positive or quality distribution is reported.

limitations: Author-stated (page 11): only two DDPM-based point-conditioned model families are studied; flow-matching, image-conditioned, closed-weight, and substantially different architectures may not share the mechanism.
Author-stated (page 11): the single-cell rescue is not a complete causal circuit because the unhealthy write alone does not induce failure and distributed signatures may remain.
Author-stated (pages 10-11): the dynamical account uses representative sphere paths and a fixed 2D projection and is not a quantitative bifurcation theorem.
Author-stated (pages 8 and 11): Make-A-Shape requires per-shape gamma search, adding many 100-step generations and leaving deployment-time parameter selection unresolved.
Author-stated (pages 8 and 11): prevalence measures the success of an adaptive adversarial search, not how often naturally acquired point clouds cause Meltdown.

Reviewer-identified: the supposedly realistic perturbations use an oracle mesh/surface for reprojection; sensor noise, occlusion, outliers, calibration error, and natural acquisition frequencies are not evaluated.

Reviewer-identified: C=1 is a binary topology proxy and can label one connected but badly distorted surface as rescued; the corpus-scale table reports no Chamfer, normal consistency, F-score, watertightness, or perceptual-quality distribution.

Reviewer-identified: Make-A-Shape is tested on only 130/1,030 GSO and 30/381 SimJEB shapes, and gamma is selected per shape against the same target outcome, making rescue rates optimistic relative to a held-out calibration policy.
Reviewer-identified: the healthy-input safety test covers one SimJEB shape and ten seeds; 40 connected outputs cannot support a general no-harm or geometry-preservation claim.
Reviewer-identified: Riesz-energy thresholds are established on spheres and do not yield a validated surface-independent detector for arbitrary real objects.
Reviewer-identified: multi-object reconstruction is shown qualitatively for one scene, leaving component identity, object separation, and scene-level generality unmeasured.

Reviewer-identified: Appendix H baselines use a small canonical sphere stress test and omit retraining, adversarial training, robust encoders, explicit uniformity regularization, and newer point-conditioned 3D systems.
Reviewer-identified: PowerRemap requires an SVD of a large 1,728 x 1,152 activation in WaLa at inference; latency, memory, numerical precision, batching, and throughput are not reported.
Reviewer-identified: no out-of-distribution detector decides when to intervene, and the full-dataset prevalence search already assumes access to healthy/failing paired endpoints.

Reviewer-identified: the claim of a basin separatrix and positive-instability-like amplification is interpretive; no Lyapunov exponent, Jacobian spectrum, Hessian, or projection-robust dynamical invariant is estimated.
failure_modes: A sparse cloud's points become slightly less uniform while remaining exactly on the surface, causing the generated mesh to split into tens or hundreds of disconnected components.
A PowerRemap gamma chosen per training-like shape fails on an unseen geometry or sampler because the relevant spectrum and site shift.
The output becomes one connected component but loses local detail, develops bridges, or deviates geometrically, so the binary rescue metric hides a harmful reconstruction.
A healthy input is unnecessarily remapped and degrades; the single-shape neutrality test is too small to bound this false-intervention rate.
A non-spherical or multi-object cloud has no meaningful Riesz threshold, so the proposed input-side diagnostic cannot identify susceptibility.
An image-conditioned, rectified-flow, or newer 3D architecture commits conditioning at a different layer/time or distributes it across sites, invalidating the WaLa patch location.
Unhealthy Y transplanted alone does not cause failure, so an intervention designed around that cell misses necessary upstream/downstream context or a redundant distributed pathway.
Full SVD latency or memory makes per-sample intervention impractical, especially for Make-A-Shape when gamma search requires repeated 100-step samples.
WLOP or aggressive input preprocessing improves a uniformity statistic but collapses local geometry and still leaves fragments, demonstrating metric gaming without reconstruction recovery.
Adding conditioning noise or choosing the best of a few samples reduces component count without crossing to C=1, producing milder but still unusable failure.
A 2D projected trajectory appears bimodal although the full state has a different topology, yielding an overstated bifurcation narrative.
Adaptive search over an oracle mesh finds a narrow pathological boundary that ordinary sensor data rarely visit, so reported prevalence overstates deployment risk.
reusable_insights: Pair activation patching with a reverse-direction noising scan; rescue sufficiency in one direction does not imply the activation alone causes the behavior.
Trace a failure from measurable input statistics through intermediate representations before searching the full denoiser, which narrows where an intervention can plausibly act.
Use matched directional and magnitude controls when interpreting spectral interventions; a correlated norm or entropy can be ruled out even when it tracks the transition closely.
Separate the basis of an activation from the basis of perturbation drift: removing leading components of the activation and removing leading drift directions test different mechanisms.
Turn mechanistic localization into a minimal test-time edit, then scan the same edit across all sites to quantify specificity rather than reporting only the successful location.
Evaluate robustness discoveries at three levels: adversarial discoverability, natural incidence, and intervention false-positive/no-harm rate; none substitutes for the others.
Report continuous geometry and topology metrics together; connected-component recovery alone cannot demonstrate faithful reconstruction.
Use trajectory ensembles instead of a single diffusion seed to distinguish a sharp deterministic transition from changing probability mass across outcomes.
Treat dynamical-systems language as a testable hypothesis and add projection-invariant quantities before calling an observed split a formal bifurcation.
Preserve negative baselines that improve intermediate diagnostics but not the target outcome; they expose where plausible preprocessing stories break.
open_questions: What is Meltdown's incidence under raw LiDAR, surgical, photogrammetric, and depth-camera point clouds with realistic occlusion, outliers, and calibration error rather than oracle reprojection?
Can a held-out, input-only detector predict failure and choose gamma without generating both healthy and unhealthy endpoints or searching against C?
What are PowerRemap's dataset-wide effects on Chamfer, normals, F-score, watertightness, local detail, and false interventions for already healthy shapes?
Does the same directional circuit exist in flow-matching, rectified-flow, image-conditioned, multimodal, and newer point-to-3D systems such as TRELLIS-based models?
Can adversarial training, point-density augmentation, encoder regularization, or architecture changes eliminate the vulnerability rather than correcting one activation at inference?
Which contextual upstream or residual-state components make healthy-to-unhealthy Y patches insufficient to induce failure, and is there a minimal bidirectional causal circuit?
Can randomized or low-rank approximate SVD deliver equivalent rescue with measured latency and bounded quality error?
Is there a geometry-general analogue of normalized Riesz energy that predicts susceptibility across arbitrary surfaces and densities?
Do projection-independent order parameters, Jacobian spectra, Lyapunov estimates, or basin-boundary measurements confirm the proposed bifurcation?
How should per-shape gamma be calibrated prospectively, and what rescue rate remains under one global or detector-selected gamma on a held-out test corpus?
Does PowerRemap preserve distinct components in legitimate multi-object scenes rather than spuriously connecting them?
Are there other catastrophic modes—holes, hallucinated bridges, topology changes without fragmentation—that component count misses but share the same circuit?

competitive_landscape.title: Wavelet Latent Diffusion (WaLa): Billion-Parameter 3D Generative Model with Compact Wavelet Encodings
competitive_landscape.relationship: audited target architecture and primary baseline
competitive_landscape.difference: WaLa introduces the billion-parameter wavelet-latent 3D generator and its point-cloud conditioning, with quality claims across generation and reconstruction. Meltdown does not replace that generator; it discovers a sparse-conditioning robustness failure inside it, localizes an early cross-attention handle, and proposes an inference-time patch. Its mechanistic conclusions therefore inherit WaLa's particular U-ViT, encoder, and DDPM design.

competitive_landscape.title: Make-A-Shape: a Ten-Million-scale 3D Shape Model
competitive_landscape.relationship: audited target architecture and transfer baseline
competitive_landscape.difference: Make-A-Shape supplies the second open point-cloud-conditioned wavelet-grid diffusion model and a ten-million-shape training scale. Meltdown demonstrates that the failure and broad spectral idea transfer, but only on small subsets and with per-shape gamma search; the tail-removal mechanism differs from WaLa's targeted drift surgery.

competitive_landscape.title: Points-to-3D: Structure-Aware 3D Generation with Point Cloud Priors
competitive_landscape.difference: Points-to-3D uses a TRELLIS-based structure-aware pipeline, inpainting, and staged sampling for object and scene generation from point-cloud priors. It postdates Meltdown's target version and is not audited there; because its architecture and generative process differ, Meltdown's single-site DDPM mechanism and PowerRemap transfer remain open rather than established across current point-to-3D systems.

competitive_landscape.title: Hunyuan3D-Omni: A Unified Framework for Controllable Generation of 3D Assets
competitive_landscape.difference: Hunyuan3D-Omni supports point clouds alongside voxels, bounding boxes, skeletons, and images in a unified controllable 3D generator. Meltdown studies only point-conditioned WaLa and Make-A-Shape and therefore contributes a deeper causal robustness case study, not evidence that its vulnerability or intervention generalizes to multimodal conditioning.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Dictionary Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: This work learns sparse dictionaries over FLUX.1 activations to identify and steer interpretable text-to-image features. Meltdown instead begins from a concrete 3D failure, uses direct activation swaps and SVD controls without a learned dictionary, and links one localized intervention to output topology and trajectory ensembles.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper uses sparse autoencoders to show early emergence, composition, prediction, and intervention of interpretable concepts in image diffusion models. Meltdown supplies a failure-specific causal localization in 3D and a spectral rescue, while its claim that early denoising commits later structure is incremental relative to this broader early-concept literature.

competitive_landscape.title: One-Step is Enough: Sparse Autoencoders for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This work trains sparse autoencoders on a single SDXL-Turbo denoising step and demonstrates interpretable causal edits and cross-model transfer. Meltdown avoids an auxiliary learned representation and instead exhaustively patches native activations around a topological failure; it offers stronger matched controls for one mechanism but much narrower model and task coverage.

competitive_landscape.title: What the DAAM: Interpreting Stable Diffusion Using Cross Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: DAAM aggregates cross-attention into attribution maps for Stable Diffusion and relates them to words and syntax, primarily correlationally. Meltdown uses paired causal activation replacement, reverse noising, and matched spectral controls to isolate a context-dependent cross-attention write tied to a concrete 3D robustness failure.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper provides the first worked connection between a single-cell causal circuit in a conditional diffusion Transformer, a low-rank directional commit variable, and a bifurcation-like split in generative trajectories, while discovering Meltdown and deriving a high-rate test-time rescue for leading point-cloud-conditioned 3D models.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The study combines adaptive on-surface stress tests across GSO and SimJEB, an exhaustive 4,864-site-per-seed activation audit, reverse-direction transplants, thousands of matched spectral controls, encoder probes, diffusion ensembles, and PowerRemap rescue rates of 97.7-98.3% for WaLa and 83.3-84.6% for tested Make-A-Shape subsets.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the unusually complete failure-to-circuit-to-intervention chain for sparse point-conditioned 3D diffusion, especially the full depth-time patch scan, directional controls, and preservation of the one-way causal asymmetry. Early-step concept control, cross-attention interpretation, and causal diffusion editing already exist, while WaLa and Make-A-Shape are the generators being audited rather than contributions of this paper. The bifurcation claim should remain 'consistent with' because it rests on one projected trajectory analysis, and the deployment claim is limited by oracle adversarial search, per-shape Make-A-Shape tuning, a binary topology outcome, and an almost nonexistent healthy-input safety sample. Overall novelty is high for mechanistic robustness case-study methodology and moderate for a general 3D defense.

reviewer_notes: Secondary verification read all 57 extracted pages, including Appendices A-H, and checked the main-to-appendix accounting for prevalence, intervention localization, directionality, dynamics, and negative baselines. Exact counts and ranges were transcribed from Table 1 and appendix tables/plots; interpretive claims are explicitly downgraded where the evidence is a fixed 2D projection, a representative shape/path, per-shape search, or a binary C metric. The audit retains the key contradiction that healthy Y rescues an unhealthy run but unhealthy Y alone never melts a healthy run. Provenance hashes match the indexed current arXiv v2 PDF/text artifacts. Eight current primary arXiv competitors were version-checked on 2026-08-23, including newer 3D systems that the target paper did not evaluate.
